ai_show_review.summary: Epic Lovelight jam & tight China>Rider transitions
ai_show_review.blurb: The show shines with a marathon Turn On Your Lovelight featuring Peter Green, plus seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider and solid performances of Black Peter and High Time. Despite early mix quirks the band stays locked in throughout.
ai_show_review.review: On February 1, 1970 at The Warehouse the Dead delivered a jam‑heavy set that still feels fresh. The centerpiece is an almost mythic Turn On Your Lovelight* where Jerry locks horns with guest guitarist Peter Green, creating a soaring dialogue that many fans cite as a highlight of the era. Earlier in the first set the classic China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue glides effortlessly, while The Other One flows into Lovelight to give the second half a looser, improvisational feel. Mid‑set gems like Black Peter and High Time keep the momentum rolling, and Pigpen’s presence adds that early‑Dead flavor. Early in the night the soundboard mix is a bit uneven—Bob’s guitar sits forward and drums are low—but once the balance settles the clarity is solid, capturing every nuance of the marathon jams.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality soundboard capture with solid overall mix after the early balance quirks; highlights the epic Lovelight and The Other One while preserving band dynamics.

key_highlights: Marathon Turn On Your Lovelight* featuring Peter Green’s guest soloing.
Seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition.
The Other One flowing into Lovelight creates a looser, jam‑heavy second half.
Strong mid‑set performances of Black Peter and High Time.

band_performance.Jerry: Trades licks with Peter Green during Lovelight, delivers great tone on Cold Rain ending and maintains solid presence once the mix settles.
band_performance.Phil: Shows early Dark Star spark; bass is low at first but becomes more present later, especially during I Know You Rider.
band_performance.Bob: Early mix pushes his guitar forward and dominates the right channel; playing is crystal clear (both good and bad notes) making him a focal point for fans.
band_performance.Mickey: Drum levels are low at the start but improve later, contributing to the evolving jam feel.
band_performance.Billy: Early drum presence is subdued; as the set progresses his playing gains clarity, though some describe the early drum segment as a bit long‑winded.
